findings.observation: Spark recurses into STRUCT/LIST/MAP before consulting Catalyst attributes. The original draft parsed these attributes; candidate 7ac8e1fe8 now skips lookup on all container kinds.
Unannotated ORC TIMESTAMP_INSTANT infers Spark LTZ. This supports schema inference only; no new real-file INSTANT runtime qualification was performed.

Spark fallback parses primitive Catalyst attributes without checking their physical ORC kind in OrcUtils.toCatalystSchema. Sail checks physical compatibility, rejects duplicate or missing primitive annotation values, unsupported primitive annotations, and decimal files lacking explicit precision or scale. These are conservative Sail supported-input limitations, not proof of identical Spark error behavior. Noncanonical TIMESTAMP spellings or TIMESTAMP_INSTANT carrying a plain timestamp annotation can also enter Spark's configured parser path; only unannotated INSTANT and Spark writer's canonical TIMESTAMP annotation are established here.

Bridge try_new builds a naive ordinary TIMESTAMP physical schema and rejects naive-to-LTZ array conversion. Qualified native timezone options instead make builder.schema infer UTC ordinary TIMESTAMP. Profile integration must derive/validate the bridge physical schema from exactly the configured native decoding mode; otherwise adapt_batch rejects the correctly configured decoded schema. Guard must remain until that integration. Native pruning suppression does not authorize Sail file/partition/statistics pruning under unqualified timestamp semantics.

Current bridge is physical-to-inferred-logical conversion, not caller-requested schema evolution. Requested names/case/missing nullable fields/projections and LTZ-NTZ compatibility belong after bridge conversion using existing ReadFormat validation hooks. Native projection is a set in physical file order; requested duplicates/reordering need a final projection. Synthetic bridge.project tests do not qualify native reordered projection.

Synthetic schema and manually constructed array tests check recursive metadata, all TIME precision bits, nulls, slicing, positional field mapping and guarded timestamps. They do not alone establish Spark runtime parity. Root's separate actual Spark ORC fixtures provide independent decoder-plus-bridge coverage for TIME and intervals/nesting, but are explicitly not registered-file-source, requested-schema, or timezone-profile integration tests. Expected semantic metadata serialized with production helper is a contract roundtrip check, not independent validation of that helper's JSON implementation.
